t: "Anytime" vs. "Any Time": A Guide of When to Use Each
s: June 13, 2024 - You can also use “anytime” as an adverb to mean “at any moment,” similar to how you’d use “at any time.” For instance, Merriam-Webster lists the sentence “The bus should be here anytime now” as correct. But if you’re using a preposition like “at,” it needs to be the two-word form; “at anytime” is incorrect.
